title: Young Child Dies of Measles in Virginia, the State's First Measles Death of 2026

content:
A young child who tested positive for measles has died in Virginia, state health officials announced Friday, Nov. 20 — the commonwealth’s first measles-associated death of 2026.

The Virginia Department of Health said the child was between 0 and 4 years old. To protect the family’s privacy, the department said it will not provide any further information about the death, including where the child lived or whether the child was vaccinated.

Virginia has reported 220 measles cases so far in 2026, including 40 among children aged 0 to 4 and 75 among children aged 5 to 12, according to state health department data as of Nov. 19. Most of the state’s cases have been in the central region.

The news came three days after a young child in the same age range tested positive for measles at UVA Health University Medical Center in Charlottesville. The health department would not say whether the two cases were linked.

A disease once thought beaten

Virginia has not had a measles-related death since 1978, according to Frederic Bertley, an immunologist and CEO of the Center of Science and Industry, who called the death alarming and evidence that measles is gaining a foothold in the United States.

The death follows a year in which the United States lost its measles elimination status, and it comes two weeks after an infant in Wisconsin died of measles — the first measles death in that state in 36 years. The Virginia health department said its measles dashboard will next be updated on Tuesday, Nov. 24.

Sources: Virginia Department of Health, Nov. 20, 2026; USA Today, Nov. 21, 2026; Reuters, Nov. 20, 2026.
